clinicalPearls: A congenital non-progressive condition in which peripheral or entire cornea resembles sclera, with loss of the normal limbal boundary
The cornea is opaque and vascularised peripherally, and the corneo-scleral junction is indistinct
It ranges from mild peripheral scleralisation to total sclerocornea with a completely opaque cornea
It is frequently bilateral and associated with other anterior segment dysgenesis and systemic malformations
Total sclerocornea causes severe visual deprivation and amblyopia
Management ranges from observation of mild cases to corneal transplantation for total involvement, with guarded results
reference.pathophysiology: Sclerocornea is a developmental anomaly of the anterior segment in which the cornea fails to differentiate distinctly from the adjacent sclera, so scleral-like opaque, vascularised tissue extends into the cornea and the limbus is ill-defined. It reflects abnormal neural crest-derived anterior segment development and often coexists with other dysgenetic features. The corneal opacification obstructs the visual axis in severe cases, causing form-deprivation amblyopia, while the abnormal anterior segment can predispose to glaucoma.
additionalInvestigations: Examination of corneal clarity and the limbal boundary
Anterior segment imaging to define the extent and associated anomalies
Intraocular pressure assessment for associated glaucoma
redFlags: Total corneal opacification threatening visual development
reference.prognosis: Mild peripheral sclerocornea has little visual impact, whereas total sclerocornea carries a poor visual prognosis even with corneal transplantation because of associated dysgenesis and amblyopia.
pitfalls: Confusing it with other causes of congenital corneal opacity
references: Taylor and Hoyt's Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus
management: Observe mild peripheral sclerocornea where the visual axis remains clear, with regular monitoring of corneal clarity and visual development
Correct any refractive error and institute aggressive amblyopia therapy with occlusion to counter form-deprivation amblyopia
Consider penetrating keratoplasty (corneal transplantation) for total sclerocornea obstructing the visual axis, counselling parents on guarded graft outcomes
Screen for and treat associated glaucoma, lowering intraocular pressure with topical antiglaucoma agents or surgery
Undertake systemic evaluation for coexisting anterior segment dysgenesis and extraocular malformations
Refer to paediatric ophthalmology and low-vision services, and offer genetic counselling given the developmental anterior segment associations
